Check whether the interviews can represent the fishing the counts measured

Source: R/interview-coverage.R
check_interview_coverage.Rd

A catch total multiplies counted effort by a catch rate from interviews, and the product is right only if the interviewed trips can represent the fishing the counts measured. The estimators check that across strata: a total refuses a stratum with counted effort and no rate, and a rate pooled across strata refuses a stratum fished with no usable interviews. Nothing in them looks within a stratum. A morning-only interview plan on a lake with an evening bite passes every one of those checks, and the rate it produces describes morning trips while the effort it multiplies covers the whole day.

Usage

check_interview_coverage(
  design,
  periods = NULL,
  fishing_hours = NULL,
  block = 60,
  use_trips = c("complete", "incomplete", "all")
)

Arguments

design

A creel_design with survey_type = "instantaneous", counts and interviews attached. Bus-route and ice designs are refused: their interviews are the effort data. Aerial and camera designs are refused: the counts there have no link to interview times.

periods

NULL, or a data frame of the periods clerks interview in, with start_time and end_time as "HH:MM": the periods table given to generate_schedule(), whose every period has a positive probability of being worked. period_id and hours columns are allowed and ignored. It may carry any of the design's strata columns to give each stratum its own periods; rows without them apply to every stratum. Any other column is refused, so a misspelt stratum cannot quietly apply a row to every stratum. Periods that vary by date (a date column, as from daylight_shifts()) are not supported yet.

fishing_hours

NULL, a character vector c(start, end) as "HH:MM" applying to every stratum, or a data frame with start_time, end_time and optionally strata columns, as for periods.

block

Block length in minutes. Default 60.

use_trips

Which interviewed trips the data layer compares: "complete" (default, the trips estimate_catch_rate() uses by default), "incomplete", or "all". A block fished only by trips the rate does not use is not covered for that rate.

Value

A creel_coverage_report, a list with:

plan

One row per stratum and block: block_start, block_end ("HH:MM" on the survey-day clock), in_fishing_day, and interviewable (TRUE, FALSE, or NA without periods and fishing_hours).

data

One row per stratum and block: mean_count, n_count_obs, interviewed_hours, n_interviews, effort_share, interviewed_share and gap.

summary

One row per stratum: n_interviews (of the trips in use_trips), n_no_clock_time, effort_share_in_data_gaps, fishing_hours_not_interviewable (minutes inside the fishing day only) and effort_share_not_interviewable.

block

The block length in minutes.

use_trips

The trips the data layer compared.

Details

check_interview_coverage() compares the two by time of day, within each stratum, in blocks of block minutes. It changes no estimate and raises no warning in the estimators; it returns a report.

Two layers, and what each can show

The plan layer asks whether a trip in each block of the fishing day had any chance of being interviewed. An access-point clerk interviews trips as they end, so a trip ending while no clerk is scheduled cannot enter the sample at all (Pollock et al. 1994; Robson and Jones 1989); a roving clerk meets anglers only while present. A block of the fishing day that no interview period overlaps has zero probability of selection, and no weighting of the trips that were interviewed can stand in for it (Lohr 2022, sec. 1.3.4). This layer can establish a gap. It needs the sampling plan, which the design does not keep: periods, the table of interview periods the schedule was drawn from, and fishing_hours, the fishing day. Without them it reports NA, never "covered".

The data layer compares, block by block, the effort the counts saw with the fishing the interviewed trips did. A count is the number of anglers present at an instant, so the mean count in a block stands for the block's effort; the interviewed fishing is the hours each interviewed trip spent in the block, from trip_start to interview_time. Time fished, not the number of interviews, is the quantity compared, because a roving clerk meets an angler with probability proportional to time fished (Hoenig et al. 1997). A block with counted anglers and no interviewed fishing is a gap. This layer can only point to a gap: in a small sample a block can be missed by chance under a plan that covers it. Hartill et al. (2011) found about 15% of boats returning after interviewers had left, a gap of exactly this kind.

What is unknown, and why it is not reported as covered

  • A block with no count in it has unknown effort: mean_count and gap are NA, not 0 and FALSE.

  • Interviews need clock times: add_interviews(trip_start = , interview_time = ). Interviews given only a trip_duration carry no time of day. While any interview in a stratum lacks one, a block with no interviewed fishing there has gap = NA, since the untimed interviews may have fished it; n_no_clock_time in the summary counts them.

  • Counts need clock times: add_counts(count_time_col = ), as "HH:MM" or date-times. Without them the data layer is NA throughout.

  • When counts were attached with period_length_col, the stored counts are already expanded by each day's period length; effort shares across blocks are then comparable only when that expansion is similar across the days a block was counted on.

Times are read on the survey-day clock, so a night creel's blocks run past midnight from its day_start.

References

Hartill, B. W., Watson, T. G., and Bian, R. (2011). Refining and applying a maximum-count aerial-access survey design to estimate the harvest taken from New Zealand's largest recreational fishery. North American Journal of Fisheries Management, 31, 1197-1210.

Hoenig, J. M., Jones, C. M., Pollock, K. H., Robson, D. S., and Wade, D. L. (1997). Calculation of catch rate and total catch in roving surveys of anglers. Biometrics, 53, 306-317.

Lohr, S. L. (2022). Sampling: Design and Analysis (3rd ed.). CRC Press.

Pollock, K. H., Jones, C. M., and Brown, T. L. (1994). Angler Survey Methods and Their Applications in Fisheries Management. American Fisheries Society Special Publication 25.

Robson, D. S., and Jones, C. M. (1989). The theoretical basis of an access site angler survey design. Biometrics, 45, 83-98.

Examples

cal <- data.frame(date = as.Date("2024-06-03") + 0:9, day_type = "weekday")
sampled <- cal$date[c(1, 3, 6, 8)]
counts <- data.frame(
  date = rep(sampled, each = 3), day_type = "weekday",
  count_time = rep(c("08:00", "13:00", "19:00"), 4),
  anglers = c(10, 8, 20, 12, 9, 25, 9, 7, 18, 11, 10, 22)
)
# Interviews only in the morning
start <- as.POSIXct(paste(rep(sampled, each = 3), "06:30"), tz = "UTC")
interviews <- data.frame(
  date = rep(sampled, each = 3), day_type = "weekday",
  catch = c(2, 1, 3, 0, 2, 1, 4, 1, 2, 3, 1, 0),
  hours = 3, status = "complete",
  trip_start = start, interview_time = start + 3 * 3600
)
design <- creel_design(cal, date = date, strata = day_type)
design <- add_counts(design, counts, count_col = anglers, count_time_col = count_time)
design <- add_interviews(design, interviews,
  catch = catch, effort = hours, trip_status = status,
  trip_start = trip_start, interview_time = interview_time
)
#> Warning: ! No `n_anglers` provided — assuming 1 angler per interview.
#> ℹ Pass `n_anglers = <column>` to use actual party sizes for angler-hour
#>   normalization.
#> ℹ If the interviews really are one angler each, pass `n_anglers = 1` to state
#>   that and silence this warning.
#> ℹ 2 interviews have zero catch.
#>   Zero catch is usual; check it is not missing data recorded as 0.
#> ℹ Added 12 interviews: 12 complete (100%), 0 incomplete (0%)
check_interview_coverage(
  design,
  periods = data.frame(period_id = 1, start_time = "06:00", end_time = "12:00"),
  fishing_hours = c("06:00", "21:00")
)
#> ── Interview coverage by time of day ───────────────────────
#> Blocks of 60 minutes, per stratum; complete trips.
#> 
#> weekday (12 interviews):
#>   Plan: 9 h of the fishing day not interviewable (74% of counted effort)
#>   Data: 74% of counted effort in blocks with no interviewed fishing
#> 
#> The plan layer can establish a gap; the data layer can only point to one.
#> Unknown means the inputs to decide it are missing, never covered.
